issues.legal_issue: A borrower who incurred an agricultural improvement loan in an individual capacity, or personally undertook repayment in the loan security, remains personally liable despite a later family partition or compromise allocating the secured property and debt to another family member.
material_facts: The borrower applied for and obtained the loan and offered his own half share in family property as security.
The Collector found after an inquiry that the borrower had taken the loan in his individual capacity, not as manager of the joint family.
The borrower’s loan bond bound him to discharge the liability from his property.
A later compromise between the borrower and his brother allocated the secured property and loan liability to the brother, but the Government was not a party to the compromise.
issues.conclusion: The loan was taken in the borrower’s individual capacity and he remained personally liable; in any event, even if he had borrowed as manager of the joint family, he was personally and severally liable. The Government was not bound by the compromise or the alleged partition.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 7(1) of the Land Improvement Loans Act, 1883, a loan and related charges may be recovered from the borrower and through other specified modes. The borrower’s undertaking in the taccavi bond made him personally liable, and a compromise to which the Government was not a party did not bind it. No earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: loan_recovery_appeal and borrower_obtained_loan and borrower_personally_undertook_repayment and government_not_party_to_family_compromise

predicates.loan_recovery_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal challenging collection of an agricultural improvement loan.
predicates.borrower_obtained_loan: The borrower applied for and obtained the loan.
predicates.borrower_personally_undertook_repayment: The borrower gave security containing an undertaking to discharge the loan liability from his property.
predicates.government_not_party_to_family_compromis: The Government was not a party to the family compromise allocating the secured property and debt.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges collection of an agricultural improvement loan, the borrower obtained it, personally undertook repayment, and the Government was not party to a later family compromise, the borrower remains personally liable.

issues.legal_issue: The expiry of a village attachment period does not discharge a debt that is a government sum recoverable as arrears of land revenue, and the village-restoration bar does not apply where no qualifying attachment was made.
material_facts: The unpaid loan was recoverable as arrears of land revenue under the applicable loan-recovery provision.
The village was not in fact attached under the statutory village-attachment procedure, and the required notification making that procedure applicable had not been issued.
The recovery sought was for the balance of the loan and interest, rather than arrears of land revenue due in respect of the village.
issues.conclusion: Section 289(2) did not bar the recovery proceedings. It applies to a qualifying village attachment and discharges liability for land revenue due in respect of the village; it does not discharge liability for other sums recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 288 and 289(1)–(2) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, govern recovery of sums recoverable as arrears of land revenue and the attachment and restoration of villages. Section 289 applies only where section 243(1) has been made applicable by notification under section 243(2). Read in context, section 289(2) discharges land-revenue liability for the village, not liability for other recoverable government dues. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.loan_recovery_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal challenging collection of an agricultural improvement loan.
predicates.debt_is_other_government_sum_recoverable: The amount sought was a government debt recoverable as arrears of land revenue, rather than land revenue due in respect of the village.
predicates.no_qualifying_village_attachment: The village had not been attached through the applicable statutory procedure.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges collection of a government debt recoverable as arrears of land revenue and no qualifying village attachment occurred, the village-restoration period does not bar recovery of that debt.

issues.legal_issue: The restoration protection for a leased holding does not bar recovery before the lease period has expired.
material_facts: The borrower argued that the leased holding had to be restored free of claims after the statutory lease period.
The recovery proceedings began before the period of the lease had expired.
issues.conclusion: The borrower was not relieved of liability under section 291(3), because the lease period had not expired when recovery proceedings were initiated.
issues.legal_principle: Section 291(3) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, provides for restoration of a holding free of the State Government’s claim for arrears in respect of that holding upon expiry of the lease period. The protection had not yet arisen because the lease period remained unexpired. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.loan_recovery_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal challenging collection of an agricultural improvement loan.
predicates.recovery_started_before_lease_expiry: The recovery proceedings began while the period of the lease had not yet expired.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges recovery that began before the lease period expired, the lease-restoration protection does not bar recovery.

issues.legal_issue: Deduction of an agricultural improvement loan from compensation is an additional mode of recovery and does not make compensation the exclusive source of payment.
material_facts: A portion of the borrower’s compensation had already been adjusted toward the loan.
The pending recovery proceedings concerned the remaining loan balance and interest.
The borrower argued that the Government could recover the outstanding amount only from compensation.
issues.conclusion: Section 6(e) provided an additional mode of recovery, not the only mode, and the Government could pursue other legally available modes for the remaining dues.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(e) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, makes amounts due under the Land Improvement Loans Act payable forthwith and permits their deduction from compensation, without prejudice to other modes of recovery. The word “may” makes deduction an available option rather than an exclusive remedy. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.loan_recovery_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal challenging collection of an agricultural improvement loan.
predicates.compensation_deduction_is_authorized: The governing arrangement permits the loan debt to be deducted from compensation payable to the borrower.
predicates.loan_balance_remains_after_deduction: A balance of the loan, including associated charges, remains after compensation has been applied.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges collection of an agricultural improvement loan, compensation may be applied to the debt, and a balance remains, other available recovery modes remain open.

issues.legal_issue: A writ court need not grant a request for an account of rents and profits where the request is not pursued and would require resolution of disputed facts.
material_facts: The borrower faintly argued that the Government should account for rents and profits from land it had let out.
The borrower did not pursue that argument further.
The High Court had examined the accounts and found that they were maintained as required by the applicable loan rules.
The requested relief involved disputed questions of fact.
issues.conclusion: The requested accounting relief was not available in the writ proceeding, particularly because it involved disputed questions of fact.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that such relief was not open to the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution, particularly where it involved consideration of disputed questions of fact. It also noted that the argument was not pursued and that the accounts had been maintained as required by the taccavi rules. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_loan_recovery: The proceeding included a writ challenge to recovery of an agricultural improvement loan.
predicates.accounting_claim_involves_disputed_facts: Resolving the request for an account would require deciding disputed facts about rents and profits.
predicates.accounting_argument_not_pursued: The borrower raised the accounting argument but did not pursue it further.

issues.definition: When a writ challenge to loan recovery includes an accounting claim involving disputed facts that the borrower does not pursue, the writ court need not grant accounting relief.
